raster.note: five GeoTIFFs on one grid; NoData (255) covers dry ground, open water and everything the SLOSH grid does not reach alike; classes 0 and 99 do not occur

method: Each of the five category rasters (EPSG:4269 NAD83 geographic, cells of 0.0000898315 degrees, about 10 m; elevation model resampled by the publisher to about 9 m) is read whole. For every building centroid and every asset the value of the one cell that contains the point is taken (nearest cell; classes are never interpolated or smoothed). Point coordinates are WGS84 and are used as NAD83 without a datum shift (about 1 m, a tenth of a cell). Values: 1..21 are the publisher's one-foot bins of inundation above ground, in feet (class n = n-1 to n ft, 21 = more than 20 ft); 0 means the cell is NoData; 255 means the point lies outside the raster. Water level is the SLOSH maximum of maximums (MOM) for the category at high tide with SLOSH+SWAN wave setup, minus ground elevation; it is a near worst-case composite, not one storm. Overlay tiles: each class cell is placed in the zoom-13 Web Mercator pixel that contains its centre and the pixel keeps the deepest class; every lower zoom is the 2 x 2 maximum of the zoom above; pixels are then coloured by the NHC viewer's four depth groups (classes 1-3, 4-6, 7-9, 10 and above). QA counts: "inundated" = class 1..21; "above 3 ft" = class 4 or more (the 3 to 4 ft bin and deeper), "above 6 ft" = class 7 or more, "above 9 ft" = class 10 or more.

classes.0: the point is inside the raster and its cell is NoData in the source: no inundation is mapped there for this category. The source does not distinguish dry ground from open water or from ground its SLOSH grid does not reach, so this is "nothing mapped", not a statement that the place is safe.
classes.99: Levee Areas (the publisher: consult local officials for flood risk); none in the Puerto Rico files
classes.255: the point is outside the raster's extent: no information

disclaimer: The data and maps in this tool illustrate the height of possible storm surge flooding under certain scenarios, and do not account for erosion, subsidence, sea-level change or future construction. Water levels are based on storm surge scenarios in the referenced SLOSH MOM tide scenario. The data, maps, and information provided should only be used as a tool for general education/awareness of the storm surge hazard at a city/community level (not for a parcel level/grid cell assessment). The SLOSH MOM storm surge risk data used to create these maps are constrained by the extent of the SLOSH grids and users should be aware that risk due to storm surge flooding could extend beyond the areas depicted in these maps. This map should not be used to replace the maps used for hurricane evacuation zones. Hurricane evacuation zones are drawn at a local and state level and consider additional information and specific criteria for a particular region in addition to the storm surge hazard. Users are urged to consult local officials for flood risk inside the hatched areas marked as leveed areas in the map. The data and maps in this tool are provided "as is", without warranty to their performance, merchantable state, or fitness for any particular purpose. The entire risk associated with the results and performance of these data is assumed by the user. This tool should be used strictly as a planning reference and storm surge risk awareness tool and not for navigation, permitting, legal, or regulatory purposes. Any conclusions drawn from the analysis of this information are not the responsibility of the National Weather Service, National Hurricane Center, Office for Coastal Management, or its partners.

disclaimer_es: (Traducción no oficial hecha por Garita; rige el texto original en inglés de NOAA.) Los datos y mapas de esta herramienta ilustran la altura de la posible inundación por marejada ciclónica bajo ciertos escenarios, y no toman en cuenta la erosión, el hundimiento del terreno, el cambio en el nivel del mar ni la construcción futura. Los niveles de agua se basan en escenarios de marejada ciclónica del escenario de marea SLOSH MOM referido. Los datos, mapas e información provistos deben usarse únicamente como herramienta de educación y concienciación general sobre el peligro de marejada ciclónica a nivel de ciudad o comunidad (no para una evaluación a nivel de parcela o de celda de la cuadrícula). Los datos de riesgo de marejada ciclónica SLOSH MOM usados para crear estos mapas están limitados por la extensión de las cuadrículas SLOSH, y el riesgo de inundación por marejada ciclónica podría extenderse más allá de las áreas representadas en estos mapas. Este mapa no debe usarse para reemplazar los mapas de zonas de desalojo por huracán. Las zonas de desalojo por huracán se trazan a nivel local y estatal y consideran información adicional y criterios específicos de cada región además del peligro de marejada ciclónica. Se exhorta a consultar a los funcionarios locales sobre el riesgo de inundación dentro de las áreas rayadas marcadas como áreas protegidas por diques en el mapa. Los datos y mapas de esta herramienta se proveen "tal cual", sin garantía sobre su desempeño, comerciabilidad o idoneidad para algún propósito particular. Todo el riesgo asociado con los resultados y el desempeño de estos datos lo asume el usuario. Esta herramienta debe usarse estrictamente como referencia de planificación y de concienciación sobre el riesgo de marejada ciclónica, y no para navegación, permisos ni fines legales o reglamentarios. Las conclusiones que se deriven del análisis de esta información no son responsabilidad del Servicio Nacional de Meteorología, el Centro Nacional de Huracanes, la Oficina para el Manejo Costero ni sus socios.
